title: Roman Authority
summary: Roman authority shaped the political setting of much of the New Testament through governors, soldiers, taxation, courts, and imperial power.
background: The New Testament often takes place under Roman oversight, which helps explain trials, public order, citizenship appeals, crucifixion, and the movement of the gospel through the empire.
teachingHelp: When Rome appears in a passage, look for issues of authority, witness, suffering, citizenship, and God’s sovereignty over rulers.
sources: International Standard Bible Encyclopedia, original 1915 edition.
